-157.89000,21.35960.name: Tripler Army Medical Center IVF Institute
-157.89000,21.35960.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Gary Levy, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-0.06455,51.34241.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to IVF London. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-36.09032,-9.78222.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://reproferty.com.br/. 28.32280,-15.38750.name: National Biosafety Authority Zambia
28.32280,-15.38750.desc: Zambia refused engineered food aid during the 2002 famine, on the grounds that accepting grain would put engineered genes into its seed stock and close its European market. The decision is still argued over, and it established that a country might weigh trade access against immediate need. In July 2002 the government refused 27,000 tonnes of World Food Programme maize in grain and milled form both, closing the compromise other governments in the region accepted; villagers looted the warehoused maize before it could be removed. The refusal was made with no biosafety law to make it under, and this Authority exists because of what followed.

28.32280,-15.38750.name: COMESA — regional biosafety policy
28.32280,-15.38750.desc: A regional biosafety policy covering nineteen African states, intended to let countries rely on a single assessment rather than each conducting its own. Regional harmonisation is how a country with no biosafety capacity gets a functioning system, and it is also how one country's decision becomes eighteen others' without a separate debate in any of them.

-90.12000,36.74200.name: Bader Farms
-90.12000,36.74200.desc: The peach farm that filed the first dicamba drift lawsuit against the seed company in 2016, and became the bellwether trial for a multidistrict litigation that has drawn in over a hundred farmers, with a crop damage class action and a separate antitrust complaint running alongside it. It is on this map for a reason the case reports do not state plainly: the farm was not a customer of the technology at issue, had no contract with either company, and grew a crop the trait was never designed for. A bellwether plaintiff in this field is often someone with no commercial relationship to the industry at all — which is who ends up carrying the burden of establishing whether a release was negligent.
